name: pheidippides-marathon-run
description: Legend says a Greek runner raced to Athens with news of victory over the invading Persians, then collapsed.

name: cursus-publicus-founded
description: Rome's first emperor set up an official system of riders, wagons and way stations to carry state messages.

name: mongol-yam-relay-network
description: The Mongol Empire formalised a vast chain of horse stations letting riders carry orders across Asia at great speed.

name: beacon-chain-armada-warning
friendly_name: Beacon Fires Warn of the Armada
description: A chain of hilltop bonfires carried news of the approaching Spanish fleet across England within hours.

name: royal-mail-opens-to-public
friendly_name: Royal Mail Opens to the Public
description: A king allowed ordinary people to send letters through the royal postal service, for a fee set by distance.

name: first-mail-coach-bath-london
description: Fast, guarded coaches replaced slow post-boys on a trial route between two English cities, speeding letters.

name: chappe-semaphore-line
description: Towers with movable arms relayed coded signals from hilltop to hilltop, sending news across a country in minutes.

name: cooke-wheatstone-telegraph
description: Two Englishmen patented a needle telegraph that pointed to letters, soon strung alongside railway lines.

name: pony-express-launches
description: Riders changing horses at relay stations raced mail across the American West between Missouri and California.

name: rural-free-delivery-begins
description: American farm families got mail delivered to their roadside boxes instead of travelling to town to collect it.

name: marconi-transatlantic-radio-signal
description: An Italian inventor received a faint Morse letter sent by wireless across the Atlantic Ocean.

name: first-official-airmail-flight
description: A pilot carried sacks of letters by aeroplane at an Indian exhibition, the first officially sanctioned mail flight.

name: cher-ami-pigeon-message
description: A wounded carrier pigeon flew through gunfire to save a trapped battalion and became a wartime hero.

name: transatlantic-radiotelephone-service
description: Callers in London and New York could speak across the ocean by radio telephone, at a very high price.

name: china-clipper-pacific-airmail
description: A giant flying boat carried airmail from California to Asia, opening regular air service over the Pacific.

name: tat-1-transatlantic-telephone-cable
description: An undersea cable carrying dozens of voice circuits replaced radio links between Europe and North America.

name: zip-codes-introduced
friendly_name: ZIP Codes Come to American Mail
description: The US post office introduced five-digit codes to speed the sorting of letters by machine.

name: dhl-express-courier-founded
description: A small San Francisco company began flying shipping documents to Hawaii, starting an international express network.

name: fedex-first-deliveries
description: A new company flew its first overnight packages from Memphis to cities across the United States.

name: western-union-ends-telegrams
description: The company that once dominated the telegraph quietly stopped sending telegrams, ending a long era of wired messages.

name: amazon-first-drone-delivery
friendly_name: Amazon Delivers a Parcel by Drone
description: An online retailer completed its first customer delivery by unmanned aircraft, carrying a parcel to a rural home.
